We are looking for young film critics! 
Cinekid is looking for English-speaking children between 4 - 14 years to join 'Ask Your Audience' in smaller focus groups. We are looking for young film critics! 
During Cinekid for Professionals this October, international filmmakers get the opportunity to present their new projects to the most important audience: kids themselves. 'Ask Your Audience' is a unique opportunity for children who love storytelling and movies, to have a real impact on the films and shows they will be watching in the future. 
 Who are we looking for? 
We are looking for English-speaking children or school groups between the ages 4 to 14. They will be joining smaller focus groups, depending on their age. After a quick presentation by selected filmmakers, kids will have the opportunity to ask questions about anything related to the project as well as share their opinions. A moderator will guide the sessions, to support a valuable exchange between the filmmakers and their young critics. 
 When and where will it happen? 
Ask Your Audience will take place during Cinekid Festival at Pathé Amsterdam Noord on 21, 22 and 23 October . Children will join us for 1 - 2 hours, depending on their age. We will share a more detailed schedule closer to the event. 
 What can we offer? 
To thank the children for their feedback, we can offer them the full Cinekid Festival experience; a complementary ticket for a festival screening and access to the MediaLab. 
 How can you apply? 
If your child is interested in participating or you would like to get more information about the programme, please contact us at professionals@cinekid.nl with the subject 'Ask Your Audience 2025'. Please include the age of your child and sign up before 24 September.

 Introduction 
The Scholar Meeting of International Tax Researchers (ScholarMIT) is an annual gathering in our Amsterdam Headquarters where early-career tax scholars can discuss their ongoing projects amongst contemporaries in the field. 
 Description 
The Scholar Meeting of International Tax Researchers (ScholarMIT) is designed for early-career tax scholars who have obtained their PhD and are under the age of 50. 
This event, held at the IBFD Head Office in Amsterdam on 1-2 February 2027, provides a dynamic platform for researchers to discuss their ongoing projects, receive expert coaching, and exchange innovative ideas with colleagues from around the world. What is the eligibility criteria? 
A maximum of 12 researchers will be admitted, selected based on the quality and originality of their research. We are looking for applicants who: 
• Applicants must spend at least 30% of their work time on research-related activities. 
• Be developing an innovative research project on international, European, or comparative taxation. 
• University professors and lecturers are particularly encouraged to apply. How do you apply? 
Upload a short CV, a synopsis of your research ( use this template ), and your PhD certificate at this link by 1 September 2026. 
• Selected participants will be announced by 15 September 2026. 
• Final materials are due by 1 December 2026. Venue 
IBFD office, Amsterdam

Looking for a stable production job with good pay where you work with your hands? We are hiring Production Workers for the Core Making department at MGG in Tegelen. In this department, you produce sand cores that are used to make high-quality aluminum castings for industries like automotive, energy, and medical equipment. This is a hands-on job in a 3-shift system, including night shifts. This job is a good fit if you: Live near Tegelen and have your own accommodation and transport Have experience working in a 3-shift system (or at least night shifts) Speak English, German, or Dutch Experience as a Production Worker or Operator is a plus, but motivation and reliability are more important. What you get: €20.18 gross per hour including allowances (see below how it is calculated) Full-time job of 37,5 hours per week in 3 shifts Travel allowance Long-term, stable work Chance of a permanent contract in the future Opportunity to develop your technical skills How is the salary calculated? The basic hourly wage is €16.06. You receive a 120% surcharge for all hours worked, whether you work the early, late, or night shift. €16.06 x 120% = €19.27. In addition, you also receive €0.91 in ADV per hour worked: €19.27 + €0.91 = €20.18 gross per hour. As a Production Worker in the Core Making department, you will: Prepare sand mixtures used for making cores Operate machines that produce sand cores Check the quality of produced cores Report deviations or issues to your supervisor Perform basic maintenance on machines Keep your workplace clean and safe Work together with colleagues to keep production running smoothly This is active, physical work where precision is important. Perfect for people with experience as: Production worker Factory worker Metalworker Construction worker Important This job is: In a 3-shift system including night shifts (06:00–14:00 / 14:00–22:00 / 22:00–06:00) Physical production work Apply now and become part of the team at MGG in Tegelen!
